newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ High Court awards against Utilicorp NZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ High Court awards against Utilicorp NZ.

text.p: A New Zealand High Court judge on Friday ordered Utilicorp NZ to forfeit NZ$50,000 of future dividends from Power New Zealand Ltd for failing to disclose a put agreement with local authorities holding 6.86 percent of Power NZ.

The verdict was in a suit by unlisted Mercury Energy, which is waging a takeover battle with Utilicorp NZ for Power NZ. The judge said Utilicorp NZ, which is 79 percent owned by Utilicorp United Inc, must also pay Mercury $50,000 costs.
Mercury currently holds 32.4 percent of Power NZ and Utilicorp holds 28.7 percent in its own right.
The judge, in a written decision, said an order would be issued directing Power NZ not to pay Utilicorp the first NZ$50,000 of future dividends it would otherwise have received.
He directed that the $50,000 should instead be distributed pro rata to Power NZ's remaining shareholders (including Mercury) at the time.
